thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency breach detected for /v1/stream (region: us-west-2). p95=420ms, p99=2.8s, error-rate increase +0.6%. Instance group: gpu-pool-7. Trigger: latency_slo_p99>2000ms for 5m.
Alex (oncall): seeing it, jumping in. Paging SRE rotation.
SRE rotation: I'm on it, thanks. Any customer-facing impact reported yet?
Priya: Not yet from Support but internal dashboards show a spike of streaming stalls labeled "kv-miss + stall". Several long tails from node gpu-node-7b.
Jamie: I pulled the slow traces. Most long requests correlate with streams pinned to accelerator a100-7 on gpu-node-7b. Kernel logs show repeated ECC correctable errors around 03:12:xx. Could be thermal thrashing.
Marcus: tagging @infra-bot for hardware telemetry. Please attach fan/temp and NVML logs.
infra-bot: Collected telemetry snapshot for gpu-node-7b (ts: 2026-03-15T03:15:02Z). GPU temps: [78C, 82C, 88C, 85C]; ECC_Correctable: 42 events in last 1h; power draw spiked then throttled. Suggested immediate: drain workloads from node, soft-evacuate, and route streaming requests away from pool-7.
Alex (oncall): plan: 1) mark node read-only, 2) drain active sessions with graceful fallback, 3) shift traffic to pool-5 variants, 4) run live mitigation script to lower concurrency on remaining nodes. Priya, can you coordinate the drain and fallback config?
Priya: doing it now. Running drain command:``` ./infra/drain-node --node gpu-node-7b --grace-period 60s --force-stream-fallback ```
Jamie: while draining, patch the runtime routing policy to prefer model-quant1 (smaller kv-caches) to reduce memory pressure. Config snippet I pushed to prod-configs: ```routing.policy.pool-7.prefer = model-quant1; routing.policy.pool-7.fallback = model-quant2```
Marcus: rolling the routing change, will monitor. Also scheduling a thermal cooloff: increasing fan curve via ipmi to avoid immediate re-throttle. Command: ```ipmitool raw 0x30 0x30 0x01 0x00``` then set curve.
SRE rotation: Drain progress: 6/12 sessions gracefully shifted, 4 sessions retried to fallback model, 2 long-lived streams still bound to node (attempting forced handoff).
Alex (oncall): For the two stubborn streams, enable forced reconnect with sticky-session timeout 20s. Add customer-notice if any session fails over. Jamie, add a temporary guardrail to avoid cascading retries.
Jamie: added guardrail: max-retries=1, backoff=250ms. Pushing now.
infra-bot: Drain complete. Node gpu-node-7b is at 95% idle, no new allocations allowed. Telemetry: temps falling to [62C, 65C, 68C]. ECC events rate decreasing but still above baseline.
Priya: marking incident severity P1 due to sustained p99 breach and potential customer latency impact. Drafting short customer notification for Support.
Alex (oncall): Good. Compose short blurb for status page: include affected endpoint, mitigation, guidance, ETA for root cause. Priya please post to #status once we have confirmation traffic normalized.
Priya: Post draft: "We experienced elevated streaming latency on /v1/stream (us-west-2) due to a degraded GPU node showing ECC and thermal throttling. Traffic rerouted and node drained; we have mitigations in place to restore p99 within minutes. Investigating hardware replacement and long-term mitigations." Any edits?
Marcus: add note: "no data loss, fallbacks ensured continuity".
Priya: updated and posting to internal #status-drafts.
Jamie: p99 improving — now 980ms (was 2.8s). p95 steady ~180ms. Error-rate back to normal. Continue to monitor for 30m.
Alex (oncall): Keep node quarantined. Next actions: 1) run nvml diagnostics, 2) schedule replacement for accelerator a100-7, 3) add stronger ECC alerting, 4) review batching and KV cache eviction heuristics to avoid future tail amplification during partial node degradation. Assign owners?
Marcus: I'll handle the hardware follow-up and ticket RMA with colo. Ticket created: HW-4521.
Jamie: I'll lead runtime tuning and alert updates (follow-up: reduce p99 alert threshold sensitivity to avoid noise, but keep critical ECC rate alert).
Priya: I'll finalize customer message and update status page after confirmation that p99 < 1s for 10m.
SRE rotation: handoff to next oncall in 30m. Logging timeline and actions in incident doc.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: severity=P1 acknowledged by Alex (oncall). Tags: gpu, thermal, ecc, streaming-latency. Incident channel locked to participants to reduce noise.
Alex (oncall): thanks all. Closing loop: if p99 rebounds we re-open and consider immediate node replacement. Monitoring continues. :thumbsup:
